claim.why_it_matters: The continued sub-entry of LC_TIME and the headword LEADING phrase are merged onto one line, and the whole right column loses its sub-entry indentation, so sub-entries (e.g. 'INSPECT statement 515', 'Qualified 96') are indistinguishable from headwords. Informative index only.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 940 (folio 916), right column, top: 'SET statement, locale 574' is indented as LC_TIME's continued sub-entry (LC_TIME 74, 435 ends the left column), then the headword 'LEADING phrase' sits flush left with the indented sub-entries 'INSPECT statement 515' and 'SIGN clause 388', then the headword 'LEAP-SECOND directive 61'. The markdown at page-940.md has '   SET statement, locale 574 LEADING phrase' on one line, then a blank line, and the rest of the right column (from 'INSPECT statement 515' to 'Alphanumeric 84') all carries the same 3-space indent with no   sub-entry markers. The left column does keep its   markers. So the two lines really are merged and the headword/sub-entry hierarchy really is lost in the right column. For example, 'Qualified 96' under LINAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER, and 'Data 133'/'Object 200' under 'Life cycle', can no longer be told apart from headwords. This is a transcription defect in the informative index, not a wrapping or formatting artifact. It changes which entry a locator belongs to, but it has no normative effect.
